transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-12-09
Start time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sara Martinez (BlueOak Head of Data), Evan Cole (BlueOak ML Eng), Maya Patel (BlueOak Security)

Summary: Short alignment on quality eval plan for POC. Focus on golden prompt set (50-100), regression test harness, hallucination checks, format validation, and scoring rubric (0-5 + pass/fail thresholds). Plan baseline benchmarks for both 2k and 4k token sequences and measure latency/throughput and token cost.

Topics covered: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey, hi everyone, thanks for coming. I'm Jordan Liu, AE at Redwood. We're here to scope the POC quality eval plan, um, and make sure we capture your success criteria.
[00:15] Sara: Thanks Jordan, hi all. I'm Sara. We're hoping the POC shows both quality improvements vs our current in-house model and predictable latency under load. Key stakeholders are product and privacy.
[00:30] Priya: Great, Priya here. I'll own the eval artifacts and run the baselines. Quick clarifying q: what's the target seq length distribution you care about? average vs tail?
[00:45] Evan: Mostly 512-2k in production, but we have a significant subset of long docs — about 15% of requests hit 3k-4k tokens because of long history + notes. So we want to test both the 2k and 4k buckets.
[01:05] Maya: From security, we need KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency notes. We'll review Redwood's SOC2 docs.
[01:20] Jordan: Good. For success criteria, can we capture both quality and SLOs? e.g., quality target is X pass rate on golden prompt set, latency < 800ms p95 for 2k tokens, and < 1.6s p95 for 4k tokens — just placeholders, we can refine.
[01:40] Sara: That sounds sensible. For quality we'd like a human-judged pass rate of 85% on core clinical extraction prompts and less than 5% hallucination incidents on structured outputs.
[02:00] Priya: Ok so we'll build a golden prompt set. Plan: 50-100 golden prompts covering extractions, summarization, and instruction-following. Each golden prompt will have an expected output example and a tolerance for variations. We'll run automated scoring plus a small human review sample to calibrate the rubric.
[02:25] Evan: For regression tests, can we include both unit-level prompts and batch-level smoke tests? Also want to track token-level diff metrics so we can see where answers drift.
[02:40] Priya: Yes, include unit tests (golden set) and regression suite that runs nightly during POC on the baseline model and any candidate variants. We'll version the prompt set and record model outputs with metadata (model version, prompt id, seed).
[03:00] Sara: About hallucination checks — we need both factuality checks and schema/format validation. For structured outputs, e.g., JSON fields, we'll enforce schema and fail if format invalid. For hallucination detection, maybe combine heuristics + reference-based checks for where we have ground truth.
[03:20] Priya: Agreed. Plan to run: 1) format validation (JSON schema), 2) hallucination heuristics (low confidence tokens, citations), 3) targeted factual checks for content with available ground truth. We'll flag items as major/minor regressions.
[03:45] Jordan: On scoring approach, propose a two-part score: automated similarity/QA metric (e.g., exact match, ROUGE-like, token overlap) normalized to 0-5 plus a human utility score 0-5. Combined weighted score (0.7 auto + 0.3 human) to produce pass/fail. Thoughts?
[04:10] Evan: That weighting seems reasonable; but we want to cap false positives where the automatic metric looks good but humans say it's wrong. So maybe add a hard check on hallucination incidents that fails regardless of combined score.
[04:30] Priya: We'll add a gating rule: any hallucination incident above threshold -> fail. Also will track regression deltas across candidate models; we'll surface top offending prompts.
[04:50] Sara: Timelines — we're targeting a 4-week pilot, ideally start next week. Week 0: agree on prompts & sample data. Week 1: baseline runs and initial QA. Week 2: candidate model runs and regressions. Week 3: human review and iterate, Week 4: final report and decision. Is that realistic?
[05:15] Jordan: Yes, sounds realistic. Redwood can run baseline in 48-72 hours once you share the sample set and credentials. There will be an initial throughput benchmark (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec) with both hosted and dedicated configs.
[05:35] Evan: About workload sizing — our average qps is 12 during peak, spiky bursts up to 45 qps for short periods. We want to see sustained throughput and burst behavior. Can Redwood simulate that?
[05:50] Priya: We can run load tests that mirror your qps distribution. For Dedicated pilot we'll propose a capacity plan (reserve GPUs to hit your p95 SLO). We'll recommend batching and KV-cache config to optimize cost.
[06:10] Jordan: On pricing, Jordan: I'll propose both a hosted trial and a Dedicated pilot option — hosted for speed, Dedicated if you want isolation. We'll include burst allowances.
[06:25] Maya: Security question — do you support BYOK via our KMS and HSM? We need key control and logs.
[06:35] Priya: Yes, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys in Private mode; for Dedicated we can enable KMS and audit logs. We'll send the security pack.
[06:50] Sara: For scoring, how will we calibrate human labeling? We need inter-rater agreement checks because our domain is clinical and small differences matter.
[07:05] Priya: We'll create a labeling guide and sample set for calibration. We'll do a 100-case calibration where two raters judge, compute kappa, and adjust rubric thresholds.
[07:25] Evan: For golden prompts, can Redwood provide initial seed prompts so we can iterate?
[07:30] Priya: Yes — we'll share a seed set of ~50 prompts covering extraction, summarization, reranking and few-shot instructions. You can augment with your exs.
[07:45] Jordan: Let's talk about pass/fail numbers. Sara suggested 85% pass and <5% hallucination. We'll keep that as target but label as baseline — if strict clinical constraints require higher, we'll note that.
[08:05] Sara: Correct, and for structured outputs the format failure rate must be near 0% — can't accept malformed JSON in production.
[08:20] Priya: We'll implement strict schema checks and mark any schema failure as critical.
[08:35] Jordan: Benchmarks — we'll run two classes: performance (latency, throughput, cost per token) and quality (golden prompt scoring, hallucination rate, format pass). We'll produce a spreadsheet with model variants, run metrics, and per-prompt diffs.
[08:55] Evan: Can we get per-token cost breakdown and recommendations like quantization suggestions?
[09:05] Priya: Yes, the Redwood Optimize outputs will include suggested quantization and batching parameters and estimated cost savings. We'll also report model-level cost per 1k tokens and per successful request.
[09:25] Maya: On compliance, we need retention and audit logs for user tokens. Can Redwood redact PII before sending logs?
[09:35] Priya: We support configurable logging and redaction; for Private/Dedicated we can disable request logging or redact at ingestion. We'll document options in the security pack.
[09:50] Jordan: Ok, let's capture explicit next steps and owners. (brief recap)
[10:00] Priya: Action items: I'll assemble the golden prompts, scoring rubric, and template eval harness. Jordan will send pilot pricing and scheduling. Sara/Evan will share sample dataset and spike qps info. Maya will review security doc.
[10:20] Sara: Thanks everyone. One more question: regression thresholds — how often will alerts trigger? We prefer daily automated runs with an alert if major regressions > 3 prompts or a drop in weighted score > 7%.
[10:40] Priya: Agreed. We'll configure daily runs and alert rules; we'll produce a live dashboard with per-prompt trends.
[11:00] Jordan: Great. Any other blockers?
[11:05] Evan: No blockers. We'll prepare the sample exports.
[11:10] Maya: I'll look at the security pack and confirm KMS needs.
[11:20] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the seed prompts and security docs.

End transcript.

References / shared artifacts mentioned: "BlueOak sample workload (to be shared)", "Redwood security pack (SOC2, KMS, audit log notes) - link to shared drive (will send)", "Golden prompts seed set (Redwood)"

Recap (verbatim items for CRM):
- POC duration: 4 weeks planned; baseline + candidate runs + human review.
- Success criteria: >=85% pass on golden prompts; <5% hallucination; strict schema pass for structured outputs.
- Workload sizing: 2k and 4k token buckets; peak 12 qps sustained, bursts to 45 qps.
- Benchmarks: latency p50/p95, throughput, token cost, per-prompt quality scores.
- Eval plan: golden prompts (50-100), regression suite, format & hallucination checks, combined automated+human scoring (0-5) with gating rules.

Action items (repeat):
- Priya: Share golden prompt set + eval harness by 2025-12-12.
- Jordan: Share pilot pricing and schedule by 2025-12-13.
- Evan: Export sample workloads (2k/4k slices) by 2025-12-15.
- Maya: Confirm KMS/audit constraints by 2025-12-11.
